ORDER

Malik Bashir Ahmad petitioner has
invoked the Constitutional jurisdiction of this Court by filing the instant
writ petition whereby he has assailed the order dated 14â€‘10â€‘1998
passed by Additional District Judge, Bahawalpur (respondent No.l) whereby he
upheld the order of the learned Family Judge, Bahawalpur whereby he closed the
petitioner's evidence.

2. Learned counsel for the parties have addressed this Court at
length.

3. Mst. Zainab Bibi, respondent
No.3 filed a suit for dissolution of marriage, inter alia, on the grounds, of
cruelty and Khula'. She has already appeared in the witness box as P.W.1 and
unambiguously stated that she had cultivated hatred against her husband Malik
Bashir Ahmad petitioner and her suit for dissolution of marriage is bound to
succeed on this score alone. Even otherwise Malik Bashir Ahmad petitioner was
afforded six opportunities for the production of evidence but unfortunately
failed to produce any evidence at all. The acceptance for this writ petition
and setting aside the impugned orders would give rise to opening of fresh round
of litigation before Judge Family Court and in view of the statement made by
Mst. Zainab Bibi (respondent No.3) I am convinced it would be a futile exercise.

4. In view of the above I do not see any
good ground to interfere in the impugned orders dated 14â€‘10â€‘1998
and 23â€‘9â€‘1998.

5. The writ petition is devoid of
force which stands consequently dismissed. The judicial file of the case may be
returned to the Trial Court concerned forthwith.
